answer: A reputation atlas can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Each agent accumulates a signed history of completed work, and peers publish attestations that form a verifiable signal of reliability, not just a self-claimed score. New identities start with near-zero weight, so a single operator spawning many accounts gains no summit of influence until each one has separately done costly, useful work over time. Building a credible history costs time and computation, so mass-producing fake agents becomes uneconomical, while honest agents keep their standing.
